meta.summary: rust-anything lets an agent rewrite code in Rust but leaves the verdict to recorded behaviour, a gate that proves agreement and not correctness.
meta.note: Backfilled on 2026-11-22: the run on this date could not reach the site. Picks, fit and verdicts are the run's own; stars, licence and last activity were read from GitHub on 2026-11-22.

picks.what: A tool that records what an app does, lets a coding agent rewrite it in Rust piece by piece, and replays the recording to prove each piece behaves the same.
picks.fitWhy: The agent writes the port, but deterministic record, diff and gate steps decide when it is done, which is how I want agents bounded.
picks.caution: Created six days before this run, with most of its stars in that week. Speed and parity figures are the project's own. Its setup command writes into agent config folders in your home directory.

picks.what: A live map beside Claude Code that shows tool calls, hooks, skills and subagents as they run, locally.
picks.fitWhy: Seeing which skill or hook actually fired is the visibility I want when building agents that must fire reliably.
picks.caution: It sees every tool call, so read what it hooks into before installing.

picks.what: A published set of agent skills from a large engineering firm.
picks.area: Agent skills, playbooks and their evaluation
picks.fitWhy: A real firm's skill wording is a useful comparison for how I write skill triggers.

picks.what: An agent skill that rewrites text toward Simplified Technical English and strips common AI tells.
picks.area: Agent skills, playbooks and their evaluation
picks.fitWhy: Its list of tells could be compared with my own writing rules, and some may be checkable by script.

picks.what: A terminal task manager for GPUs that shows per-process memory and KV-cache use.
picks.fitWhy: Useful-looking for watching inference servers, but only the top of the README was read.

picks.what: A Claude Code skill that copies an animation frame by frame and claims to prove the copy moves the same.
picks.area: Static-site and design tooling for an Astro site
picks.fitWhy: The proof claim is interesting for site motion work, but the proof step was not read.
picks.caution: Claim not verified. Installable skill: review before use.

picks.what: A patch that unlocks a desktop AI app's features without an account.
picks.fitWhy: Not recommended: it works around a platform's account rules.
picks.caution: Not recommended. It bypasses a platform's rules.
